chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Ali from one of the Imams, peace be upon them both.
Regarding a man who did not bid farewell to the House (Kaaba), he said: 'There is no harm if he had an excuse or was forgetful.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the House (referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.يُوَدِّعِ: to bid farewell (specifically referring to Tawaf al-Wada')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to perform the farewell Tawaf?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the farewell Tawaf is a recommended act (mustahabb) rather than an obligatory pillar (rukn), as the absence of penalty for forgetfulness or illness indicates its non-compulsory nature. This ruling distinguishes the Shia view from some Sunni schools that consider it obligatory, emphasizing that the omission does not invalidate the Hajj itself but merely removes a recommended closing ritual.
